newsitem.title: USA: Phoenix Insurance reports record 1996 surplus.
newsitem.headline: Phoenix Insurance reports record 1996 surplus.

text.p: Phoenix Home Life Mutual Insurance Company said on Monday its surplus grew to a record $1.1 billion in 1996, up 26 percent from 1995.
Phoenix Chairman Robert Fiondella also told policyholders at the annual meeting that the company's surplus-to-assets ratio grew to 12.3 percent, from 10.6 percent in 1995.
New annual premiums, which have increased by 22 percent since 1992, grew to $246.9 million in 1996, the company said.
Phoenix Duff & Phelps, a money manager which is 60-percent-owned by Phoenix, completed its first full year of operation with about $34 billion in assets under management, the company said.
Phoenix Duff & Phelps revenues grew by 36 percent to $152.5 million.
American Phoenix, the company's property-casualty broker business, continued to expand in 1996, Fiondella said.
"It, too, positioned itself to take advantage of global opportunities with the purchase of a Lloyd's of London broker and a new Miami brokerage operation focussing on Latin America," he said.
Other 1996 activities included an investment in Aberdeen Trust, an international money manager with $4 billion in assets.
Phoenix has about $40 billion in assets under management, and is the nation's 14th-biggest mutual life insurer, and one of its largest money managers.
